VIRTUAL MIDPOINTS: CONTINUOUS-TIME INFORMATION THAT SAMPLING HIDES
Solo construction, 31 October 2026. Historical priority unestablished.

1. THE MISSING OPERATION AND ITS CONTRACT

The complete discrete-time inference framework in entropy_witnesses/PROOF.txt
recovers a discrete hidden-model minimum. It does not impose continuous-time
embeddability. That limitation can erase ALL inferable dissipation: Section5
constructs a driven finite CTMC whose sampled binary process is itself an
exactly reversible Markov chain. Its discrete hidden-model minimum is zero.

Here the additional premise is stationary, time-homogeneous, reciprocal,
all-even finite CTMC dynamics, observed through a fixed binary state label
at equal physical intervals Delta. Neither its generator, hidden state count,
stationary probabilities nor mixing rate is supplied to inference. Stationary
hidden preparation and the physical time/reversal model remain external.
The target is realised FULL path entropy through N Delta, not a stationary
ensemble mean rate. Astra N185's mean-rate obstruction remains intact.

Only Y_0,...,Y_N are acquired. Let f(0)=+1,f(1)=-1 and
S_N=sum_{k<N}f(Y_k)f(Y_{k+1}). The result below uses the existence of the
hidden half-interval kernel R=exp(Delta Q/2), without observing midpoints.
More generally it applies to a stationary Markov square-root realization;
the full CTMC entropy follows by conditional Holder under path projection.

2. A RETURNING TWO-PHASE KERNEL LEMMA

Adjoin an auxiliary bit c which flips at every HALF step. Its stationary
law is uniform, its flip is a reversible involution, and its entropy is zero.
The product chain has stationary law pi times uniform and transition R times
flip. Let K be its positive entropy-tilted kernel for a bounded payoff H
satisfying the entropy cone H_s+phi*(H_a)<=0, phi(t)=2t atanh t.
The earlier proved kernel lemma gives w(K)<=exp(theta^2 M^2/2), |H_a|<=M,
for0<theta<=1/2, where w is the complex numerical radius.

The observation protocol fixes c_0=0. This initial clock law is not stationary,
but there is NO factor2 loss at an EVEN horizon: K^(2N) preserves clock phase.
For the unit vector v0=sqrt2*1{c=0} in L2(pi times uniform),

 E_{pi,c0=0} exp{theta[sum H-Sigma_halfgrid]}
      =<v0,K^(2N)v0><=w(K^(2N))<=w(K)^(2N).                (V1)

The last step is the numerical-radius power inequality already proved in
reversible_cur

THE FIRST NONTRIVIAL DIVISIBILITY LAYER IS EXACTLY SOLVABLE
Solo derivation, 31 October 2026. Builds on the preserved four-state root.

Let P_r be the COMPLETE stationary balanced binary Markov law with transition
eigenvalue-r,0<r<1: its flip probability is(1+r)/2. Define V_m as in PROOF.txt:
m times the minimum entropy per edge of a stationary standard-Borel hidden
kernel R whose observations every m steps have law P_r. Then

          V_1(P_r)=0,
          V_2(P_r)=2 phi(sqrt r)=4sqrt r atanh(sqrt r)>0.   (D1)

The second equality is an EXACT unrestricted-hidden-model result, including
the complete observed law, not a moment diagnostic or fixed hidden-count fit.

Lower bound. For any such root R, let C_j=E[f_0 f_j] at its fine grid.
C_2=-r, while its C_1 is unconstrained. Write u=Rf,v=R*f,a=(u+v)/2,t=(u-v)/2.
Then C_2=E(a^2-t^2), C_1=E(fa), and E t^2>=C_1^2-C_2>=r.
One direct derivation of e(R)>=phi(sqrt(E t^2)) uses the symmetrized edge
measure eta=(Gamma+Gamma^T)/2 and edge imbalance z=(Gamma-Gamma^T)/(Gamma+Gamma^T).
Conditional expectation gives t(x)=E_eta[z(x,Y)f(Y)|x]. Thus E t^2<=E_eta z^2.
Also e(R)=E_eta phi(z), and phi(sqrt s)=2sum_{k>=1}s^k/(2k-1) is convex
and increasing. Jensen gives e(R)>=phi(sqrt(E_eta z^2))>=phi(sqrt r).
Extended zero/support/infinite cases use the same limiting conventions as
the original entropy cone. Multiplying by2 proves V_2>=2phi(sqrt r).

Attainment. Put b=sqrt r and use the four-state kernel already constructed
in predictive_flow/PROOF.txt, states(s,t) in{+1,-1}^2, uniform stationary law:

 R((s,t),(s,-t))=(1+b s t)/2,
 R((s,t),(-s,t))=(1-b s t)/2.

It has Rs=b t, Rt=-b s and hence R^2s=-b^2s=-r s. Strong lumpability makes
the ENTIRE stride-two observed process the Markov law P_r, not just its
lag-two moment. Pairing the reciprocal edges gives e(R)=phi(b), proving
attainment in (D1). The root itself is periodic and is not claimed to be a
finite-CTMC sampled kernel. Its admissibility is at V_2's discrete-root scope.

Consequently every stationary all-even CTMC realization of P_r obeys the
sharper population lower bound

                 Delta*sigma_CT>=2phi(sqrt r).             (D2)

source_excerpts.text:
A QUANTITATIVE QUARTER-STEP POPULATION CERTIFICATE
Solo derivation, 31 October 2026. This is NOT a finite-data mean-rate bound.

The strict next-layer argument can be made quantitative. Put
g(r)=phi(sqrt r). For the law P_r in DIVISIBILITY.txt,

       V_4(P_r)>=max{2g(r), (8/5)[r+g(r)]}.               (Q1)

The second expression strictly improves V_2=2g(r) whenever g(r)<4r,
including the frozen CTMC source. It also holds using ONLY the exact
negative lag-four correlation-r of the fine binary observable; the rest
of the complete coarse law is not needed for this particular inequality.

Proof. Let R be a fine stationary Markov kernel, K=R^2, and suppose
<f,K^2f>=-r for f in{-1,+1}. Assume e(R)<infinity; otherwise trivial.
Set u=Kf,v=K*f,t=(u-v)/2,a=(u+v)/2, h=t f. Write eta for the symmetrized
K edge measure, z for its imbalance, and

 A=E_pi t^2=r+E_pi a^2>=r,
 D=E_eta z^2-A=E_eta[z(x,y)f(y)-t(x)]^2>=0,
 delta=e(K)-g(r)>=0.

Since g'(s)>=2 and e(K)>=g(E_eta z^2),

                  delta>=2(E_eta z^2-r)>=2D.              (Q2)

Let epsilon_x=z(x,y)f(y)-t(x),
epsilon_y=-z(x,y)f(x)-t(y). Antisymmetry gives
h(x)+h(y)=-epsilon_x f(x)-epsilon_y f(y). Each residual has mean square D,
so E_eta[h(x)+h(y)]^2<=4D. Stationarity and f^2=1 imply

             <h,Kh><=2D-A<=delta-r.                      (Q3)

For ANY real bounded observable |h|<=1 and stationary R,

                   e(R)>=-2<h,R^2h>.                     (Q4)

Indeed the symmetrized R flow gives e(R)>=2E z_R^2 and, by conditional
Jensen, E[(Rh-R*h)/2]^2<=E z_R^2 because |h|<=1. Adjointness gives
<h,R^2h>=E[((Rh+R*h)/2)^2-((Rh-R*h)/2)^2]. This proves(Q4), without
assuming h is binary or centered.

Apply(Q4) to h=t f, use(Q3), and then data processing e(K)<=2e(R):

 e(R)>=2r-2delta
      =2r-2e(K)+2g(r)
      >=2r-4e(R)+2g(r).

Hence5e(R)>=2[r+g(r)]. Multiplying by4 and taking the unrestricted
fine-root infimum gives(Q1). The argument remains valid when a right
side at an intermediate line is negative; no positive-part substitution
or extra case assumption is required.
